design.captured_state: last patch token of the 1280-d residual stream
design.lipschitz: L_raw = ||dh||/d; L_rel = ||dh||/(d*||h||) with ||h|| = mean of the two endpoint norms. L_rel is the primary quantity because the residual-stream norm is not a common scale across layers (tokenizer ~30-70, block 15 ~220, head ~28 at b=5) and the blocks re-normalise internally with RMSNorm.

decision_rules.P2: first layer with ratio >= 2.5 is l* > 0 and the half-max width narrows from l* to block20
decision_rules.P2_dark_band: l* = first layer whose dip argmin lies within 0.01 of the integer, with the dip depth (flank median / min of L_rel) growing toward block19 (secondary flag: depth >= 1.5)
decision_rules.P4: angle peak within 0.05 of the integer, growing with depth

design.r_readout: r(b) from sweep.retained on the 32-sample reported forecast; the fine fhat uses the same read-out on the 128-sample output patch, band-unit grid at 1/64 cycle per 32 samples
design.token_degeneracy: mean pairwise cosine of the 16 patch tokens of the sequence (the sequence-level degeneracy that is invisible to a per-token Lipschitz), at the tokenizer output and at block 20

P2_born_and_sharpens.rule: first layer with ratio >= 2.5 is l* > 0; half-max width narrows from l* to block20
P2_born_and_sharpens.no_feature_note: the ratio never exceeds the control window's, i.e. there is no localised bright band at the integer at any depth; the state trajectory is smooth through the null

P2_dark_band.rule: unpredicted counterpart: the narrow feature is a *dip* (stall) of L_rel, not a peak.  l* = first layer whose dip argmin lies within 0.01 of the integer (the tokenizer's does not); the depth (flank median / min) must then grow toward block19.  The depth threshold 1.5 is reported as a secondary flag.
P2_dark_band.norm_bump_rule: the feature is also measured directly as a narrow bump of the residual-stream NORM ||h_l(b)||: ratio = max/flank median over the window, argmax = the band of the maximum

P4_tangent_peak.rule: angle peak within 0.05 of the integer and growing with depth
